{{Short description|Canadian-American biologist}}
'''Christopher Roland Somerville''' is a Canadian-American biologist known as a pioneer of ''[[Arabidopsis thaliana]]'' research. Somerville is currently Professor Emeritus at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and a Program Officer at the [[Open Philanthropy Project]].

== Life and career ==
Somerville majored in Mathematics and completed a PhD in Genetics at the [[University of Alberta]], and then did postdoctoral research in the laboratory of William Ogren before serving as a faculty member at U. Alberta,  [[Michigan State University]],<ref name="Balzan Prizewinner Biography 1947" /><ref name="early-demonstration" /> Stanford University, and UC Berkeley. He directed the Department of Plant Biology at the [[Carnegie Institution for Science]] at [[Stanford University]] and then the [[Energy Biosciences Institute]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He retired from the UC Berkeley faculty in 2017.<ref name="cnr-retirements">{{Cite web| title = College of Natural Resources Faculty Retirements| work = UC Berkeley College of Natural Resources| accessdate = 2017-12-19| url = https://nature.berkeley.edu/news/2017/06/cnr-faculty-retirees}}</ref>

Somerville was co-founder and Executive Chairman of [[Mendel Biotechnology, Inc.]] and a co-founder of Poetic Genetics, [[LS9, Inc]], and Redleaf Biologics.<ref>{{Cite web| title = About – RedLeaf Biologics| accessdate = 2021-07-05| url = https://redleafbiologics.com/about/}}</ref>
Somerville has contributed to societal debates on the value of [[transgenic crops]]<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1104/pp.123.4.1201| issn = 0032-0889| volume = 123| issue = 4| pages = 1201–1202| last = Somerville| first = Chris| title = The Genetically Modified Organism Conflict| journal = Plant Physiology| date = 2000-08-01| pmid = 10938338| url = https://doi.org/10.1104/pp.123.4.1201| pmc = 1539266}}</ref> and biofuels.

Together with  [[Elliot Meyerowitz]], Somerville was awarded the [[Balzan Prize]] in 2006 for his work developing the small mustard plant ''A. thaliana'' as a model.<ref name="Milano Zurigo">{{cite While at Michigan State University and funded by [[United States Department of Energy|DOE]], Somerville's research included developing transgenic plants which contained genes from two bacteria and enabled Arabidopsis to produce polyhydroxybutate (PHB), a biodegradable plastic.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Andy |last=Coghlan |title=Technology: How to sow cress and reap plastic |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg13418204-000-technology-how-to-sow-cress-and-reap-plastic/ |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=New Scientist |language=en-US}}</ref> Companies already used PHB grown in bacteria, but it would be more cheaply produced from plants with the concept that potato would produce the plastic.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Feature: Farm Fields of Dreams |url=https://alumni.msu.edu/stay-informed/alumni-stories/feature-farm-fields-of-dreams |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=Alumni |language=en-US}}</ref> 

Many trainees from Somerville's lab have started independent labs, including [[Mark Andrew Estelle|Mark Estelle]], Peter McCourt, George W. Haughn, John W. Schiefelbein, [[Christoph Benning]], Clint Chapple, Wolf-Dieter Reiter, John Browse, [[Sean Cutler]], [[Dominique Bergmann]], Seung Y. Rhee, Staffan Persson, Wolfgang Lukowitz, C. Stewart Gillmor, Jose Martinez-Zapater, Hong Zhang, Ruth Finkelstein, Micha Volokita, Barbara Moffatt, Kathy Wu, Jose Botella, Bertrand Lemieux, Erwin Grill, John Shanklin, Yves Poirier, Christianne nawrath, Susan Gibson, Deane Falcone, Koh Iba, Simon Turner, Pierre Broun, [[Sean Cutler]], Joe Ogas, Wolf Scheible, Dario Bonetta, John Sedbrook, Heather Youngs, Farhah Assaad, Michelle Facette, Alex Paredez, Jose Estevez, Seth DeBolt, Thorsten Hamman, Ying Gu, Ian Wallace, Philipp Benz, Charles Anderson, and Adrienne Roeder.

Somerville is a member of the U.S. [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] (1996), the [[Royal Society]] (1991), and the [[Royal Society of Canada]] (1993). Among the awards he has received are:  the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency|EPA]] Presidential Green Chemistry Award (2010); [[Balzan Prize]] (with [[Elliot Meyerowitz]]) (2006); [[Genetics Society of America|Genetics Society]], Mendel Medal (2004); [[Biochemical Society]], Hopkins Medal (2004); [[American Society of Plant Biologists|ASPB]] Gibbs Medal (1993);  [[Humboldt Research Award|Humbolt Research Award]] (1992);  [[American Society of Plant Biologists|ASPB]] Schull Award (1987);  [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Young Presidential Investigator Award (1984). He was awarded honorary degrees by the [[University of York]] (2016); [[Michigan State University]] (2012); Guelph [[University of Guelph|University]] (2006);  [[Wageningen University & Research|Wageningen University]] (1998);  [[University of Alberta]] (1997); [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queens University]] (1993). 

=== Media Appearances ===
Appeared in the Bill Nye the Science Guy episode entitled "Pollution Solutions".<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f3WlyZrJvh8 |title=Bill Nye the Science Guy  0407 Pollution Solutions |date=2017-07-01 |last=oben04 |access-date=2025-01-18 |via=YouTube}}</ref> He presented his research on biodegradable plant-based plastics using the model plant Arabidopsis.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-16 |title=Screen scrimmage: Famous scenes shot at Stanford and Berkeley |url=https://stanforddaily.com/2023/11/16/screen-scrimmage-famous-scenes-shot-at-stanford-and-berkeley/ |access-date=2025-01-18 |language=en-US}}</ref> 

== Research highlights ==
* Pioneered ‘biochemical genetics’ approach to problems in plant metabolism, including [[photorespiration]],<ref name="early-demonstration" /> lipid metabolism, and [[cellulose]] synthesis.
* First map-based cloning of an ''A. thaliana'' gene<ref name="Arondel-1992">
{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1126/science.1455229| volume = 258| issue = 5086| pages = 1353–1355| last1 = Arondel| first1 = V.| last2 = Lemieux| first2 = B.| last3 = Hwang| first3 = I.| last4 = Gibson| first4 = S.| last5 = Goodman| first5 = H. M.| last6 = Somerville| first6 = C. R.| title = Map-based cloning of a gene controlling omega-3 fatty acid desaturation in ''Arabidopsis''| journal = Science| date = 1992-11-20| pmid = 1455229| bibcode = 1992Sci...258.1353A}}
</ref>

* Lead development of [[The Arabidopsis Information Resource]] (TAIR) database and web resource
